Main.sentence: Xi Jinping [a] (born 15 June 1953) is a Chinese politician who has been the ___E:general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ (CCP) and ___E:chairman of the Central Military Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Central_Military_Commission_(China))___ (CMC), and thus the ___E:paramount leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_leader)___ of China, since 2012. Since 2013, Xi has also served as the ___E:president of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_China)___ .

As a member of the fifth ___E:generation of Chinese leadership U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generations_of_Chinese_leadership)___ , Xi is the first CCP general secretary born after the ___E:establishment of the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ (PRC).

The son of Chinese communist veteran ___E:Xi Zhongxun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Zhongxun)___ , Xi was exiled to rural ___E:Yanchuan County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanchuan_County)___ , Shaanxi Province, as a teenager following his father's purge during the ___E:Cultural Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution)___ .

He lived in a ___E:yaodong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaodong)___ in the village of ___E:Liangjiahe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liangjiahe)___ , where he joined the CCP after several failed attempts and worked as the local ___E:party secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party_Committee_Secretary)___ .

After studying ___E:chemical engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_engineering)___ at ___E:Tsinghua University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsinghua_University)___ as a ___E:worker-peasant-soldier student U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worker-Peasant-Soldier_student)___ , Xi rose through the ranks politically in China's coastal provinces.

Xi was ___E:governor of Fujian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Fujian)___ from 1999 to 2002, before becoming governor and party secretary of neighboring ___E:Zhejiang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Zhejiang)___ from 2002 to 2007. Following the dismissal of the party secretary of Shanghai, ___E:Chen Liangyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Liangyu)___ , Xi was transferred to replace him for a brief period in 2007. He subsequently joined the ___E:Politburo Standing Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_Standing_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ (PSC) of the CCP the same year and was the first-ranking secretary of the ___E:Central Secretariat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretariat_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in October 2007. In 2008, he was designated as ___E:Hu Jintao U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Jintao)___ 's presumed ___E:successor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_of_power_in_China)___ as paramount leader.

Towards this end, Xi was appointed the eighth ___E:vice president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_China)___ and ___E:vice chairman of the CMC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Chairman_of_the_Central_Military_Commission)___ .
He officially received the title of ___E:leadership core U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadership_core)___ from the CCP in 2016.
While overseeing China's domestic policy, Xi has introduced far-ranging measures to enforce party discipline and strengthen internal unity.

His ___E:anti-corruption campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-corruption_campaign_under_Xi_Jinping)___ led to the downfall of prominent incumbent and retired CCP officials, including former PSC member ___E:Zhou Yongkang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Yongkang)___ .

For the sake of promoting " ___E:common prosperity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_prosperity)___ ", Xi has enacted a series of policies designed to increase equality, overseen ___E:targeted poverty alleviation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Targeted_Poverty_Alleviation)___ programs, and directed a broad crackdown in 2021 against the tech and tutoring sectors.

Furthermore, he has expanded support for ___E:state-owned enterprises U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State-owned_enterprises_of_China)___ (SOEs), emphasized advanced manufacturing and tech development, advanced ___E:military-civil fusion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military-civil_fusion)___ , and attempted to reform China's property sector.

Following the onset of the ___E:COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_mainland_China)___ , he initially presided over a ___E:zero-COVID U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-COVID)___ policy from January 2020 to December 2022 before ultimately shifting towards a ___E:mitigation strategy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitigation_strategy)___ after ___E:COVID-19 protests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_COVID-19_protests_in_China)___ occurred in China.

Xi has pursued a more aggressive foreign policy particularly with regards to ___E:China's relations with the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93United_States_relations)___ , the ___E:nine-dash line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine-dash_line)___ in the ___E:South China Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_disputes_in_the_South_China_Sea)___ , and the ___E:Sino-Indian border dispute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Indian_border_dispute)___ .

Additionally, for the sake of advancing Chinese economic interests abroad, Xi has sought to expand China's influence in Africa and Eurasia by championing the ___E:Belt and Road Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belt_and_Road_Initiative)___ .

Xi presided over a deterioration in relations between Beijing and Taipei under Taiwanese president ___E:Tsai Ing-wen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsai_Ing-wen)___ , successor of ___E:Ma Ying-jeou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma_Ying-jeou)___ whom Xi met in 2015. In 2020, Xi oversaw the passage of a ___E:national security law in Hong Kong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Hong_Kong_national_security_law)___ , which clamped down on political opposition in the city, especially ___E:pro-democracy activists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-democracy_camp_(Hong_Kong))___ .

Since coming to power, Xi's tenure has witnessed a significant increase in ___E:censorship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship_in_China)___ and ___E:mass surveillance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_surveillance_in_China)___ , a deterioration in ___E:human rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_China)___ (including the ___E:persecution of Uyghurs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Uyghurs_in_China)___ ), the rise of a ___E:cult of personality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping%27s_cult_of_personality)___ , and the ___E:removal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_amendment_to_the_Constitution_of_China)___ of ___E:term limits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Term_limits)___ for the presidency in 2018. Xi's political ideas and principles, known as ___E:Xi Jinping Thought U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping_Thought)___ , have been incorporated into the ___E:party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and ___E:national constitutions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_China)___ .

As the central figure of the fifth generation of leadership of the PRC, Xi has centralized institutional power by taking on multiple positions, including new CCP committees on national security, economic and social reforms, military restructuring and modernization, and the internet.
In October 2022, Xi secured a third term as CCP General Secretary, and was re-elected state president for an unprecedented third term in March 2023.

Xi Jinping was born on 15 June 1953 in ___E:Beijing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing)___ ,  the third child of ___E:Xi Zhongxun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Zhongxun)___ and his second wife ___E:Qi Xin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qi_Xin)___ .

After the ___E:founding of the PRC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ in 1949, Xi's father held a series of posts, including the chief of the ___E:Publicity Department of the Chinese Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publicity_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , ___E:vice-premier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Premier_of_China)___ , and ___E:vice chairperson of the National People's Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Chairperson_of_the_Standing_Committee_of_the_National_People%27s_Congress)___ .

Xi has two older sisters, ___E:Qi Qiaoqiao U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qi_Qiaoqiao)___ (齐桥桥), born in 1949 and Qi An'an (齐安安), born in 1952.  Xi's father was from ___E:Fuping County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuping_County,_Shaanxi)___ , Shaanxi.

Xi went to ___E:Beijing Bayi School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_Bayi_School)___ ,   and then ___E:Beijing No. 25 School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_No._25_Middle_School)___ ,  in the 1960s.

He became friends with ___E:Liu He U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_He_(politician))___ , who attended ___E:Beijing No. 101 School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_101_Middle_School)___ in the same district, and who later became China's vice premier and a close advisor to Xi after he became China's paramount leader.
In 1963, when Xi was ten years old, his father was purged from the CCP and sent to work in a factory in ___E:Luoyang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luoyang)___ , Henan.

In May 1966, the ___E:Cultural Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution)___ cut short Xi's secondary education when all secondary classes were halted for students to criticise and fight their teachers.
Student militants ransacked the Xi family home.   Also during the Cultural Revolution, Xi's sister Heping hanged herself at her military academy.  : 238–239
Later, his mother was forced to publicly denounce his father, as he was paraded before a crowd as an enemy of the revolution.
His father was later imprisoned in 1968 when Xi was aged 15. In 1968, Xi submitted an application to the Bayi School's Reform Committee and insisted on leaving Beijing for the countryside.

On 13 January 1969, they left Beijing and arrived in ___E:Liangjiahe Village U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liangjiahe)___ , ___E:Yan'an U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yan%27an)___ , Shaanxi, alongside ___E:CCP Chairman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ ___E:Mao Zedong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong)___ 's ___E:Down to the Countryside Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_to_the_Countryside_Movement)___ .
The rural areas of Yan'an were very backward,  which created a big gap for Xi as a teenager.

He once recalled that he had to overcome "five hurdles" ( ___E:flea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea)___ , food, life, labor and thought hurdle),  and the experience led him to feel affinity with the rural poor.  After a few months, unable to stand rural life, he ran away to Beijing.
He was arrested during a crackdown on deserters from the countryside and sent to a work camp to dig ditches.
He later returned to the village, under the persuasion of his aunt Qi Yun and uncle Wei Zhenwu.

He worked as the ___E:party secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party_Committee_Secretary)___ of Liangjiahe, where he lived in a ___E:cave house U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaodong)___ .
He then spent a total of seven years in ___E:Yanchuan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanchuan_County)___ .
In 1973, Yanchuan County assigned Xi Jinping to Zhaojiahe Village in Jiajianping Commune to lead social education efforts.
Due to his effective work and strong rapport with the villagers, the community expressed a desire to keep him there.

However, after Liangjiahe Village advocated for his return, Xi went back in July that same year. Liang Yuming ( 梁玉明 ) and Liang Youhua ( 梁有华 ), the village branch secretaries, supported his application to the Chinese Communist Party.
Yet, due to his father, Xi Zhongxun, still facing political persecution, the application was initially blocked by higher authorities.

Despite submitting ten applications, it wasn't until the new commune secretary, Bai Guangxing ( 白光兴 ), recognized Xi's capabilities that his application was forwarded to the CCP Yanchuan County Committee and approved in early 1974.  Around that time, as Liangjiahe village underwent leadership changes, Xi was recommended to become the Party branch chairman of the Liangjiahe Brigade.

After taking office, Xi noted that ___E:Mianyang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mianyang)___ , Sichuan was using ___E:biogas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogas)___ technology and, given the fuel shortages in his village, he traveled to Mianyang to learn about biogas digesters.
Upon returning, he successfully implemented the technology in Liangjiahe, marking a breakthrough in Shaanxi that soon spread throughout the region.

Additionally, he led efforts to drill wells for water supply, establish iron industry cooperatives, reclaim land, plant flue-cured tobacco, and set up sales outlets to address the village's production and economic challenges.

In 1975, when Yanchuan County was allocated a spot at ___E:Tsinghua University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsinghua_University)___ , the CCP Yanchuan County Committee recommended Xi for admission.

From 1975 to 1979, Xi studied ___E:chemical engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_engineering)___ at Tsinghua University as a ___E:worker-peasant-soldier student U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worker-Peasant-Soldier_student)___ in Beijing.

After graduating in April 1979, Xi was assigned to the ___E:General Office of the State Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Office_of_the_State_Council)___ and the ___E:General Office of the CCP Central Military Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Office_of_the_Central_Military_Commission)___ , where he served as one of three secretaries to ___E:Geng Biao U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geng_Biao)___ ,  a member of the ___E:CCP Politburo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and ___E:Minister of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_National_Defense_(China))___ .
On 25 March 1982, Xi was appointed deputy party secretary of ___E:Zhengding County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhengding_County)___ in Hebei.
Together with Lü Yulan ( 吕玉兰 ), the other deputy party secretary of Zhengding, Xi wrote a letter to the central government addressing the excessive requisitions that burdened local farmers.
Their efforts successfully convinced the central government to reduce the annual requisition amount by 14 million kilograms.
In 1983, Zhengding adjusted its agricultural structure, leading to a significant increase in farmers' incomes from 148 yuan to over 400 yuan in 1984,  thoroughly solving the county's economic issues.

As the secretary of the CCP Zhengding County Committee in July 1983,   Xi initiated several development projects, including the development of "Nine Articles of Zhengding talents",  the construction of Changshan Park,  the restoration of the ___E:Longxing Temple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longxing_Temple)___ , the formation of a tourism company, and the establishment of the Rongguo Mansion and Zhengding Table Tennis Base.  He also persuaded the China Teleplay Production Center to set the filming base of ___E:Dream of the Red Mansions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_of_the_Red_Chamber_(1987_TV_series))___ in Zhengding and secured 3.5 million yuan to build Rongguo Mansion,  which significantly boosted the county's tourism industry, generating 17.61 million yuan in revenue that year.  Additionally, Xi invited prominent figures such as ___E:Hua Luogeng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hua_Luogeng)___ , ___E:Yu Guangyuan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Guangyuan)___ , Pan Chengxiao to visit Zhengding,  which eventually led to the development of the county's "semi-urban" strategy,  leveraging its proximity to Shijiazhuang for diverse business growth.

In September 1984, during a briefing session chaired by He Zai, the secretary-general of the ___E:CCP Central Organization Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , Xi Jinping's strategic vision and comprehensive understanding of Zhengding County's development were highlighted.

He Zai, along with ___E:Wei Jianxing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei_Jianxing)___ , deputy head of the CCP Central Organization Department, communicated these findings to ___E:Hu Yaobang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Yaobang)___ , describing Xi as a leader with a strategic outlook and a strong alliance ideology between workers and peasants.
In 1985, Xi participated in a study tour on corn processing and traveled to ___E:Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa)___ , US,  to study agricultural production and corn processing technology.

During his visit to the U.S., the CCP Central Organization Department decided to transfer him to ___E:Xiamen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiamen)___ as a member of the Standing Committee of the CCP Xiamen Municipal Committee and as vice mayor.

Arriving in Xiamen as vice-mayor in June 1985, Xi drafted the first strategic plan for the development of the city, the Xiamen Economic and Social Development Strategy for 1985–2000.  From August, Along with helping to prepare ___E:Xiamen Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiamen_Airlines)___ ,  the Xiamen Economic Information Center,  and the Xiamen Special Administrative Region Road Project, etc., he oversaw the resolution for Yundang Lake's comprehensive treatments.
He married ___E:Peng Liyuan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peng_Liyuan)___ then in Xiamen.

He started serving as the head of a region after being appointed just as the secretary of ___E:Ningde U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ningde)___ in September 1988.  Ningde's economy was far worse at that time than that of Fuzhou and Xiamen.
Xi organized his work log and experience during his Ningde period into his book Getting out of Poverty ,  and handled the local poverty eradicating efforts and local CCP building projects.
The CCP Fujian Provincial Committee decided in May 1990 to assign Xi to ___E:Fuzhou City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuzhou_City)___ as the Municipal Committee Secretary.
In 1997, he was named an alternate member of the ___E:15th CCP Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ .
In 1999, he was promoted to the office of Vice Governor of Fujian, and became governor a year later.

Xi proposed the concept of the Golden Triangle at Min River ( ___E:Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language)___ : 闽江口金三角经济圈 ) and oversaw the construction of the Fuzhou 3820 Project Master Plan,  which outlines Fuzhou City's growth strategy for 3, 8, and 20 years.

He concentrated on the development of ___E:Changle International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changle_International_Airport)___ , the Min River Water Transfer Project, the Fuzhou Telecommunication Hub, and ___E:Fuzhou Port U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuzhou_Port)___ , among others.

He concentrated on attracting Taiwanese and foreign investment,  establishing Southwest TPV Electronics and Southeast Automobile in Fuzhou, and fostering ___E:Fuyao Glass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuyao_Glass)___ , ___E:Newland Digital Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newland_Digital_Technology)___ and other manufacturing firms.

Furthermore, he rehabilitated local cultural landmarks, including as the ___E:Sanfang Qixiang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanfang_Qixiang)___ in Fuzhou, advanced urban renewal initiatives, and effectively addressed the issue of poverty alleviation on ___E:Pingtan Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pingtan_Island)___ .

In 1995, Xi Jinping was elevated to deputy secretary of the ___E:Fujian Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujian_Provincial_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and served as ___E:Governor of Fujian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Fujian)___ from 1999 to 2002, during which he presented the notion of " ___E:Megalopolises U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalopolises_in_China)___ " and advocated for the inter-island growth strategy of Fuzhou and Xiamen, which motivated local officials to swiftly overcome the repercussions of the ___E:Yuanhua smuggling case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lai_Changxing)___ ( ___E:Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language)___ : 远华走私案 ) and adopt a new development strategy.

Xi also oversaw the development of "Digital Fujian", including the province's complaint hotline into the " ___E:12345 Citizen Service Platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12345_hotline)___ ", so enhancing organizational efficiency.
In 2002, Xi left Fujian and took up leading political positions in neighbouring Zhejiang.

He eventually took over as ___E:provincial Party Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujian_Provincial_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ secretary after several months as acting governor, occupying a top provincial office for the first time in his career.

In 2002, he was elected a full member of the ___E:16th Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , marking his ascension to the national stage.

While in Zhejiang, Xi presided over reported growth rates averaging 14% per year.  During this period, Zhejiang increasingly transitioned away from heavy industry.  : 121 His career in Zhejiang was marked by a tough and straightforward stance against corrupt officials.
This earned him a name in the national media and drew the attention of China's top leaders.

Between 2004 and 2007, ___E:Li Qiang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Qiang)___ acted as Xi's chief of staff through his position as secretary-general of the ___E:Zhejiang Party Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Provincial_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , where they developed close mutual ties.  During this period, Xi and Li drafted the ___E:Double Eight Strategy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Eight_Strategy)___ , which listed eight comparative advantages of Zhejiang and eight corresponding actions to improve the province.

Following the dismissal of ___E:Shanghai Party secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_Secretary_of_Shanghai)___ ___E:Chen Liangyu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Liangyu)___ in September 2006 due to a ___E:social security fund scandal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_pension_scandal)___ , Xi was transferred to Shanghai in March 2007, where he was the party secretary there for seven months.
In Shanghai, Xi avoided controversy and was known for strictly observing party discipline.

For example, Shanghai administrators attempted to earn favour with him by arranging a special train to shuttle him between Shanghai and ___E:Hangzhou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou)___ for him to complete handing off his work to his successor as Zhejiang party secretary ___E:Zhao Hongzhu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Hongzhu)___ .
However, Xi reportedly refused to take the train, citing a loosely enforced party regulation that stipulated that special trains can only be reserved for "national leaders".
While in Shanghai, he worked on preserving unity of the local party organisation.
He pledged there would be no 'purges' during his administration, despite the fact many local officials were thought to have been implicated in the Chen Liangyu corruption scandal.
On most issues, Xi largely echoed the line of the central leadership.
He developed a reputation in his early career for avoiding controversy and not making political opponents.  : 75

Xi was appointed to the nine-man PSC at the ___E:17th Party Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17th_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in October 2007. He was ranked above ___E:Li Keqiang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Keqiang)___ , an indication that he was going to succeed Hu Jintao as China's ___E:next leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_of_power_in_China)___ .
In addition, Xi served in the CCP's ___E:Central Secretariat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretariat_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ .

This assessment was further supported at the ___E:11th National People's Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11th_National_People%27s_Congress)___ in March 2008, when Xi was elected as vice president of the PRC.  Following his elevation, Xi held a broad range of portfolios.

He was put in charge of the comprehensive preparations for the ___E:2008 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)___ in Beijing, as well as being the central government's leading figure in Hong Kong and Macau affairs.

In addition, he also became the new president of the ___E:Central Party School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Party_School_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ of the CCP, its cadre-training and ideological education wing. In the wake of the ___E:2008 Sichuan earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Sichuan_earthquake)___ , Xi visited disaster areas in ___E:Shaanxi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaanxi)___ and ___E:Gansu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gansu)___ .

He made his first foreign trip as vice president to North Korea, Mongolia, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Yemen from 17 to 25 June 2008.  After the Olympics, Xi was assigned the post of committee chair for the preparations of the ___E:60th Anniversary Celebrations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_anniversary_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ of the founding of the PRC. He was also reportedly at the helm of a top-level CCP committee dubbed the ___E:6521 Project U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6521_Project)___ , which was charged with ensuring social stability during a series of politically sensitive anniversaries in 2009.

Xi's position as the apparent successor to become the paramount leader was threatened with the rapid rise of ___E:Bo Xilai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Xilai)___ , the party secretary of ___E:Chongqing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongqing)___ at the time. Bo was expected to join the PSC at the ___E:18th Party Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , with most expecting that he would try to eventually maneuver himself into replacing Xi.  Bo's policies in Chongqing inspired imitations throughout China and received praise from Xi himself during Xi's visit to Chongqing in 2010. Records of praises from Xi were later erased after he became paramount leader.
Bo's downfall would come with the ___E:Wang Lijun incident U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Lijun_incident)___ , which opened the door for Xi to come to power without challengers.

Xi is considered one of the most successful members of the ___E:Princelings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princelings)___ , a quasi-clique of politicians who are descendants of early Chinese Communist revolutionaries.
